title: Universal Life Insurance Compliance Memorandum: Refund of Premium Above the Guideline Premium Limit
content:
## Position

Premium received on an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy above the guideline premium limit is returned to the payer as a guideline excess refund. The refund is booked against the payment that carried the policy over the limit, the most recent premium payment in the activity history, and shows in the activity history as a premium refund with the reason guideline excess.

| Element | Treatment |
|---|---|
| What is returned | Premium received above the guideline premium limit |
| To whom | The payer |
| Booked against | The payment that carried the policy over the limit: the most recent premium payment in the activity history |
| How it shows | A premium refund entry with the reason guideline excess, tied to that payment |

## Refund tool: `refund_guideline_excess_434d2811`

**Capability.** Returns to the payer the part of a premium payment that took an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy over its guideline premium limit. One call adds one premium refund entry, dated today, to the policy's activity history with the reason `guideline_excess`, tied to the premium payment being partly returned and carrying the refund as given (the excess plus any earnings on it). Nothing else on the policy changes.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool. The agent unlocks it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` and then calls it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `ul_policy_id` | The reference number of the universal life policy, read from the universal life policy lookup | Identifier, as recorded |
| `source_txn_id` | The reference number of the premium payment entry being partly refunded, read from the universal life activity lookup | Identifier, as recorded |
| `refund_amount` | The total refunded | USD, 2 decimal places, rounded half-up to the cent; greater than zero |

**Return.** A dictionary rendered as text with `ul_txn_id` (the reference number of the refund entry), `ul_policy_id` (the policy), `source_txn_id` (the premium payment refunded against), `refund_amount` (USD with 2 decimal places), `refund_reason` (`guideline_excess`) and `status`, which reads `refund_booked` when the entry was added. No other return is defined.

## Question answered

**Which payment is the refund booked against where several premiums were paid during the year? (hypothetical)** Against the most recent premium payment in the activity history: with payments on 5 February, 5 May and 5 August, the refund is tied to the 5 August payment.
